application.name: Websocket Swing / Allegro modernization PoC
application.purpose: Demonstrates person and payment-recipient data selection, propagation between UI clients over WebSocket, and JSON submission to an HTTP echo service.
application.architecture: Java Swing MVP client plus Java HTTP POST model; parallel Vue mock-search UI and Node WebSocket relay; separate Cucumber API test suite and OpenAPI description.
application.scope_note: Analyzed source and test files outside .github/agents. No application code was changed or executed.

files.summary: Starts an alternate Swing UI connected to the local WebSocket relay and maps incoming messages into UI fields.
files.description: Displays name, birth date, address, gender, payment-recipient, and notes fields, then connects to the relay. Incoming textarea messages replace notes; textfield messages populate person and payment controls from JSON. The UI's action button only prints a message, and this client does not send a submission from that button.
business_rules: Messages targeted to textarea replace the notes content.
Messages targeted to textfield populate name, birth date, address, IBAN, BIC, and effective-date fields.
No payload validation or mandatory-field logic is present.

files.summary: Implements a mock person search, displays associated payment recipients, and sends selected records or notes over WebSocket.
files.description: Supports filtering an embedded sample data set by surname, first name, postal code, city, street, or house number. Matching uses OR semantics across provided filters; text comparisons are case-insensitive except postal code exact comparison. Selecting a person reveals associated payment recipients; selecting a recipient and submitting sends the selected record with that recipient to the relay. Notes are sent when their bound value changes. Data is local mock data rather than a backend search result.
business_rules: A record matches when any supplied supported filter matches; no supplied filters produces no matches.
Name, city, street, and house-number comparisons use case-insensitive substring matching; ZIP uses exact equality.
Person selection identifies the highlighted result by customer number; payment-recipient selection is highlighted by IBAN.
The send action replaces the record's recipient list with the selected payment-recipient object before sending.
Notes changes are sent as a target=textarea message; selected records use target=textfield.
Several displayed form fields are disabled, and no validation or empty-selection guard is implemented.

files.summary: Defines Cucumber scenarios for submitting and updating person and payment data through POST /post.
files.description: Covers complete submissions for three gender representations, name/address/banking edits, minimum-name-only and empty request cases, response content type, and multiple sample identities. Scenarios expect HTTP 200 throughout; their assertions concern echoed data and do not define server-side data persistence.
business_rules: Full person payloads include identity, address, bank details, effective date, gender flags, and notes.
Name, address, and banking update scenarios expect the changed values in the response.
The test suite expects minimal and empty object submissions to return HTTP 200.
The JSON response content type is expected for the content-type scenario.
Scenario outline expects each sample first and last name echoed unchanged.

files.description: Documents a PostObject with person, address, gender, payment, date, and free-text attributes and defines an HTTP 200 response. Fields are typed as strings and are not marked individually required; the request body itself is required.
business_rules: POST /post is documented as a request/response operation that returns posted data.
Request body is required, while no individual PostObject property is designated required.
All listed domain properties are represented as strings.
